title: Brook's Quickfire 91 Puts England in Command as Four Batters Hit Fifties Against Pakistan
excerpt: England close day two at Headingley on 366-8, leading Pakistan by 195 runs after Harry Brook, Joe Root, Jordan Cox, and Dan Lawrence all pass 50.
body:
• England reached 366-8 on day two of the first Test at Headingley, establishing a first-innings lead of 195 runs over Pakistan's 171.
  • Harry Brook top-scored with 91 off just 93 balls, hitting 13 fours after being dropped on 1, but fell nine short of what would have been his first home-ground century.
  • Joe Root (66), Jordan Cox (73 on his second Test appearance), and Dan Lawrence (51 in his first Test in two years) all made half-centuries without converting.
  • Ali Usman claimed 5-92 — his maiden Test five-wicket haul and the first by a visiting spinner at Headingley since Ashley Mallett in the 1972 Ashes.

Harry Brook punished Pakistan for a crucial early drop with a blistering 91 that put England firmly in control of the first Test at Headingley. But the world's top-ranked Test batter and three of his teammates will all be rueing missed chances after none of four half-centurions managed to convert on a rain-shortened second day.

Brook Makes Pakistan Pay

Dropped on just 1 by stand-in captain Salman Ali Agha diving at second slip off Khurram Shahzad, Brook proceeded to dismantle a lightweight Pakistan seam attack. The 27-year-old Yorkshireman struck 13 fours in an innings that came off just 93 balls, taking his average against Pakistan across 12 Test appearances above 85.

https://x.com/thetimes/status/2090686897978777731

What set this knock apart from Brook's typical pyrotechnics was its composure. Playing in England's first Test of the post-Bazball era following Ben Stokes' retirement and Brendon McCullum's departure as coach, Brook was less flamboyant but no less punishing, hardly offering another chance until Ali Usman snuck an arm ball through his defenses late in the day.

It was the second time Brook had been dismissed in the 90s at his home ground — he made 99 against India here last year — and would have been his first Test century at Headingley and 11th overall in 39 matches.

Root and Cox Lay the Platform

The base for England's dominant position was built by Joe Root and Jordan Cox in a third-wicket stand of exactly 150. Root made 66 — his 109th Test innings of 50 or more — before playing across a straight ball from Khurram Shahzad to be trapped lbw.

Cox, given his chance at number three after Jacob Bethell's knee injury, seized it with both hands. Appearing in just his second Test, the 24-year-old hit Khurram for seven fours in the space of 12 balls on his way to 73, a maiden Test half-century. He fell misjudging a full delivery from Usman and was caught behind.

"Probably one of us could have kicked on and instead of making just a hundred, make it 150, 160, 170 and that puts us in a better position definitely."

— Jordan Cox, after stumps on day two

Lawrence Returns in Style

Dan Lawrence, recalled after two years in the international wilderness to fill the considerable boots left by Stokes at number six, made 51 from 79 balls. He and Brook shared a fifth-wicket partnership of 120 that effectively killed the contest as a fair fight. Lawrence top-edged a sweep off Usman to end an innings that suggested the selectors may have found a long-term solution to their biggest vacancy.

Usman's Historic Five-For

The sole bright spot for Pakistan was Ali Usman's 5-92. The left-arm spinner's maiden Test five-wicket haul was historic — the first by a visiting spinner at Headingley since Australia's Ashley Mallett during the 1972 Ashes. Usman dismissed Brook, Cox, Lawrence, Gus Atkinson, and Ollie Robinson, with the last two falling to successive deliveries in the 80th over.

Pakistan, who last won a Test in England eight years ago, face a daunting deficit. With better weather forecast for the remaining three days, England will look to push the lead past 250 and give their seam bowlers time to finish the job.

What It Means for India Watchers

The match carries implications for India's Test planning. Brook's extraordinary record against Pakistan — built largely during the 2022 tour of the subcontinent — offers a blueprint for the kind of positive batting that has troubled Pakistan's bowling attacks. With India's own series against Pakistan a fixture cricket fans perpetually anticipate, Brook's method against spin will be closely studied in subcontinental coaching circles.

England will resume on day three looking to wrap up their innings quickly and put Pakistan under sustained pressure.
